instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line a large baking sheet with parchment.
In a large bowl, whisk together 2 cups of the flour, the cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda, sugar and salt.
Cut the cold butter into 1/2 inch chunks. Add them to the bowl and rub them into the flour with your fingertips, until it looks like coarse sand with some pea-sized pieces of butter left.
Pour in 3/4 cup of the buttermilk and stir until a shaggy dough forms. If it looks dry, add the rest of the buttermilk a tablespoon at a time. Stop as soon as there are no dry patches.
Dust the counter with a little of the remaining flour. Turn the dough out and pat it into a rectangle about 3/4 inch thick.
Cut the rectangle into thirds, stack the pieces and pat it out to 3/4 inch thick again. Do this once more.
Dust a sharp knife with flour and cut the dough into 12 squares. Press straight down and don't twist.
Set the squares on the baking sheet and bake for 13 to 15 minutes, until golden on top and deep golden on the bottom.

To keep a batch for later, freeze the cut squares on the baking sheet until solid, then move them to a freezer bag, where they keep for 3 months. Bake them straight from frozen at 425°F, adding a few minutes. Baked and cooled biscuits freeze the same way. Reheat them from frozen in a 350°F oven until warm.
method_notes: Once Upon a Chef's flaky buttermilk biscuits (4.93 from 223 ratings) is the lead, including the cornstarch and the two fold-and-pat turns. The freezer notes come from the same page and agree with the freezer-biscuit pages found in search. The list's jam is not on the ingredient list.
